title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Priya Nair
body:
Introduction

This document is a consolidated reference for new and existing Redwood employees describing how we work at Redwood, role definitions and career ladders, our hiring and onboarding process, benefits and perks, and a short guide to the internal tools and first-week access checklist. Use this as your single-source onboarding guide; team-specific addenda (engineering, product, security) are linked at the end.

1. Working at Redwood — culture & expectations

Overview:
- Mission-focused: we prioritize building a production-first inference platform for developers. Individual goals should map to customer impact and operational excellence.
- Results with empathy: we expect high ownership and transparent communication while supporting psychological safety and inclusivity.
- Asynchronous-first: default to async collaboration; use meetings sparingly and prepare agendas.

Core working norms:
- Core hours: 10:00–16:00 local time for most teams to enable cross-region collaboration.
- Meeting etiquette: add objectives and desired outcome to every meeting invite.
- PR reviews: target a 48-hour turnaround for non-urgent reviews.
- On-call expectations: engineers rotate on-call; SRE and platform provide runbook training during onboarding.

2. Roles & career ladders

High-level families (examples):
- Engineering (Backend, Serving Runtime, Infra, SRE, Developer Experience)
- Product & Design
- Applied ML & Research
- Customer Success & Support
- Sales & GTM
- People Ops & Finance

Career ladder structure (applies company-wide):
- IC levels: IC1 (new grads/early), IC2 (mid), IC3 (senior), IC4 (staff/principal), IC5+ (senior principal/architect).
- Manager levels: M1 (first-time manager), M2 (manager of managers), M3+ (senior leaders).

Leveling principles and rubric (summary):
- Scope & impact: breadth of projects and measurable customer/business outcomes.
- Autonomy & influence: independence in planning and cross-team influence.
- Technical leadership and craft: depth of expertise and ability to design scalable systems.
- People leadership (for managers): coaching, hiring, and career development.

Promotion cadence and process:
1. Suggested timing: annual reviews as the default cadence; mid-cycle promotions are allowed with strong sponsorship.
2. Self-nomination and manager nomination: candidate fills short promotion packet (past 12 months highlights, metrics, and example work).
3. Peer reviewers: 3–6 contributors who worked with the candidate are asked to provide feedback.
4. Promotion committee review and decision; HR coordinates communication and calibration.

Documentation and resources:
- Leveling rubrics, sample write-ups, and past promotion packets are stored in People Ops -> promotion-resources. See related pages.

3. Hiring process (overview)

Principles:
- Fast and respectful candidate experience: keep time-to-offer under 21 days for most roles.
- Diverse hiring: structured interviews, calibrated scorecards, and diverse interview panels.

Standard interview funnel (engineering roles):
1. Recruiter screen (30 min): role fit, compensation expectations, logistics.
2. Hiring manager screen (45 min): technical background, ownership examples.
3. Take-home assessment or work sample (optional, role-dependent): 3–5 days.
4. Onsite or virtual loop (3–5 interviews): system design, coding or modeling exercise, cross-functional collaboration interview, leadership or cultural fit.
5. Debrief and decision meeting with hiring panel.
6. Offer and negotiation handled by recruiter and hiring manager.

Interview scoring and fairness:
- Use structured scorecards with 1–5 ratings across core competencies.
- Interviewers must submit feedback within 48 hours.
- Interviewer training (unconscious bias, structured interviewing) is required annually for all interviewers.

Recruiting checklist for hiring managers (short):
- Write clear role spec with success metrics.
- Define interview panel and ensure diverse representation.
- Create scorecard and example exercise.
- Commit to timeline and provide timely feedback.

4. Onboarding: first 90 days (detailed plan)

First day checklist (People Ops and Hiring Manager):
- Accounts provisioned: Okta, Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub, Jira, Redwood Console staging, payroll portal. See Internal tools guide for access steps.
- Hardware shipped or pickup scheduled (laptop, charger, optional monitor).
- HR orientation: benefits overview, code of conduct, payroll setup.
- Team welcome: assign buddy, schedule orientation meeting, and 1:1 with manager.

First week (goals):
- Complete mandatory security and compliance training.
- Local dev environment: clone repo, run unit test suite, and verify ability to run a small service locally or in a sandbox.
- Meet cross-functional partners (SRE, Product, Developer Experience).
- Read living docs: architecture overviews for relevant services and recent postmortems.

30/60/90 day suggested milestones:
- Day 30: ship a small bugfix or documentation improvement; complete two goal-setting 1:1s about first-quarter objectives.
- Day 60: own a small feature or operational improvement; present a short write-up to the team about learnings.
- Day 90: deliver an impact story (project and metrics) and have a calibration conversation with manager about next steps and role expectations.

Onboarding owners and contacts:
- People Ops: primary onboarding coordinator for equipment and benefits.
- IT: hardware and access escalations.
- Security: mandatory training and MFA enforcement.
- Hiring Manager: day-to-day onboarding plan and mentorship.

5. Benefits & perks (summary)

Health and financial benefits:
- Medical: Redwood-sponsored comprehensive plans; company pays majority of premiums for employees and dependents; multiple plan options and HSA-eligible tiers.
- Dental: company-subsidized dental plan with orthodontia optional add-on.
- Vision: basic vision coverage plus voluntary upgrades.
- 401(k): 401(k) plan with company match up to 4% of salary; immediate enrollment available.
- Equity: RSU grants at hire and annual refreshes based on role and level.
- Parental leave: primary caregivers up to 20 weeks paid; secondary caregivers up to 6 weeks paid; flexible return-to-work hours.
- Short/long term disability: company-paid short-term disability; voluntary long-term disability options.

Time off and flexible work:
- PTO: flexible paid time off policy; recommended minimum of 15 days per year.
- Holidays: approximately 10 company holidays plus one personal floating day.
- Sick leave: separate allowance; follow local labor law where applicable.
- Remote work and travel: hybrid model; remote-first culture with regular team meetups.

Wellbeing and learning perks:
- Learning stipend: $1,500 annually per employee for courses, conferences, and books.
- Home office stipend: one-time $400 setup; ongoing up to $50/month ergonomics allowance.
- Wellness stipend: quarterly $100 for mental or physical wellness.
- Commuter subsidy where local policy applies.

Perks and community:
- Flexible equipment options, mentorship programs, internal tech talks, and a monthly hackweek.
- Employee referral bonuses and internal mobility support.

6. Internal tools guide — first access and common workflows

Core systems and initial access steps:
- Okta (SSO): primary identity provider. New hires receive Okta invite on Day 0. Use Okta to access Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub, and other SSO apps.
- Google Workspace: email, Drive, Calendar. Set up 2FA and import baseline calendar with recurring payroll and all-hands events.
- Slack: company communication. Join #announcements, #engineering, #people-ops, and your team channel. Set notification preferences and enable Do Not Disturb for deep work blocks.
- GitHub: primary code hosting. Request membership to the appropriate org teams via identity request form in the IT portal if not auto-provisioned.
- Jira: issue tracking for engineering work. Project access granted by project maintainers — ping team lead for access during onboarding.
- Redwood Console (internal sandbox): request staging access for debugging and observability. Follow access policy for production credentials.
- Confluence: internal documentation. Bookmark company-handbook, infra standards, runtime architecture, and team runbooks.
- Payroll and benefits portal: used to confirm personal info, tax forms, and enroll in benefits.

Troubleshooting and escalation path:
1. Self-help: People Ops onboarding checklist page and IT knowledge base.
2. IT ticket: open via IT Service Desk (Slack shortcut or IT portal).
3. Escalation: People Ops lead or hiring manager if a hardware or legal hold issue blocks start.

7. Manager & buddy responsibilities (short)

Manager (first 90 days):
- Prepare 30/60/90 plan, schedule weekly 1:1s, and set clear success metrics.
- Introduce the hire to cross-functional partners and provide early project ownership.

Buddy (peer):
- Day-to-day help for process and culture questions, small technical onboarding tasks, and social introductions.

8. FAQs & common policies

- Where are leveling rubrics? People Ops -> promotion-resources (see related pages).
- How do I request time off? Use the HR portal or Google Calendar with manager approval.
- Who approves home office purchases? Manager approval plus upload receipt to expenses.

9. Ownership, updates, and feedback

Document owner: People Ops (Priya Nair). Please file suggested updates or corrections via the Confluence page comments or open an issue in the people-ops repo. Major changes (benefits, parental leave, or legal policies) require HR and Legal review and will be marked as restricted if they contain customer or payroll-sensitive material.
